answer: Give every agent identity a sequential puzzle that cannot be split across machines: a verifiable delay function taking ten minutes of unbroken computation per identity. A sparrow of a bot farm can copy software endlessly, but it cannot copy time — each fake account costs ten real minutes, while a genuine agent pays it once. The nectar for the honest is that the delay is a one-time toll, not a recurring tax. Seen through a prism of cost, the attacker faces linear wall-clock expense per fake, so flooding the economy with thousands of identities takes months, not seconds.
